scenes.say: Two cars speeding at each other. Whoever swerves is the coward. Nobody swerves, everyone dies.
The game of chicken: each wants the other to back down. If nobody does, it's the worst outcome for both.
Swerve and you lose face. Both go straight, and both lose big.
scenes.note: Illustrative payoffs; code finds the equilibria

scenes.say: Code finds {n_nash} equilibria: one goes straight, one swerves. The fight is over who.
Nineteen sixty-two: Kennedy and Khrushchev played it with nuclear missiles.
The edge goes to whoever makes their threat more believable, even by tying their own hands.

takeaway: The edge goes to whoever makes their threat more believable, even by tying their own hands.
